explanation: This slide summarizes the structural components of the light reactions: 1) Photosystem II (PS II): composed of a pigment complex and electron acceptors; it receives electrons from split water molecules and releases oxygen gas. 2) Electron Transport Chain (ETC): composed of cytochrome complexes and plastoquinone; it transfers electrons from PS II to PS I while pumping H+ from the stroma into the thylakoid space. 3) Photosystem I (PS I): contains a pigment complex and electron acceptors, positioned next to the enzyme that reduces NADP+ to NADPH. 4) ATP Synthase Complex: contains an ion channel that allows H+ to flow down their gradient, driving the enzymatic joining of ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi) to produce ATP.

questions.q: What drives the ATP synthase complex to produce ATP from ADP and Pi?

The flow of H+ through its channel

The accumulation of NADPH in the thylakoid space
